newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals slip, palladium volatile.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals slip, palladium volatile.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures settled mostly lower on Tuesday, pressured by weaker bullion prices, traders said.
Activity in palladium futures was most volatile.

Most palladium prices hit all-time highs in the morning session on short-covering by private investors, but a sharp retreat in bullion prices in the afternoon, correcting rapid price rises in recent days, sent most palladium futures into negative territory by the close.
Gold prices ranged from seven yen lower to one yen firmer. Most-active benchmark April was off two yen at 1,332 yen.

Traders said there was no special factor behind the sharp fall in spot palladium. "As the palladium price rises in recent days were too rapid, caution about the higher prices encouraged long-liquidation," one trader said.
The volatile price movements boosted volume in palladium futures. The trader said platinum group metal prices may be heading slightly lower to consolidate after recent gains.

Platinum prices also extended early losses to end lower on the heels of palladium. Benchmark April palladium was down 12 yen per gram at 599 yen. Benchmark April platinum was off six yen at 1,450 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted a tad weaker at $347.15/45 per ounce at 0810 GMT, against $347.40/90 in New York on Monday.
In gold futures market, animated mixed trade was detected.
"After gold rallied above $350 on Monday, gold prices eased back due to the dollar's rebound," one trader said.
Traders said gold would likely to move sideways for some time, with a close watch being kept on the currency market for clues to direction.
Benchmark April silver was down 1.9 yen per 10 grams at 187.6 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7431
